name: Wide Control 4-1-4-1

slots.why: The sweeper keeper joins the first line of patient build-up.
The support wing-back offers the outside width beside the wide playmaker.
The ball-playing defender starts switches toward either wide creator.
The cover defender protects the circulation structure against a direct ball; Defend is the alternate.
The right-back supports the inverted winger without racing beyond the rest-defence.
The deep-lying playmaker is the secure central outlet beneath the midfield line.
The wide playmaker creates from a deeper left starting point and draws play toward the inside channel.
The defensive central midfielder protects the left side when the playmaker roams inside.
The box-to-box midfielder connects the possession line with the lone forward and arrives to support the box.
The inverted winger joins central combinations from the right while retaining a supporting duty.
The complete forward links with the creators and supplies enough box presence for patient attacks.

description: A 4-1-4-1 that controls the ball through a Wide Playmaker and flat Inverted Winger, rather than relying on AML/AMR roles.
whyGood: It lets a technical ML/MR player dictate from wide while the 4-1-4-1 keeps a stable defensive screen behind the creators.
whyThisShape: The wide playmaker moves inside to connect with the DLP, while the inverted winger makes a second central lane. Full-backs retain conventional support duties so the flat midfield has width without losing rest-defence.
whenToUse: When your best technical players are natural ML/MR positions and you want a controlled, low-risk way to use them.
whenNotToUse: When you need constant runners beyond the striker, or when the full-backs cannot provide the width the creators leave behind.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Use short first-line outlets and midfield connections to start attacks; this asks for secure decisions under pressure.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Hold Shape: Retain the available passing structure after a regain rather than forcing an immediate counter.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
